evidence: @Controller('enrolments') and @Post() decorators from @nestjs/common: routing belongs in the presentation layer
constructor(private readonly enrolmentsService: EnrolmentsService): wiring to the application layer, which presentation may depend on
enrol(@Body() dto: EnrolDto): Promise<Enrolment> passes its fields straight to enrolmentsService.enrol(courseId, dto.studentEmail)
withdraw gets the refund value from enrolmentsService.withdraw(...) and only wraps it as { refund }; the refund decision itself is made in the service
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/enrolments/enrolments.controller.ts sits in the presentation layer, and everything in it does presentation work. It uses NestJS routing decorators (@Controller, @Post, @Body) from @nestjs/common, which is what a presentation layer should do. The constructor injects EnrolmentsService, which belongs to the application layer. Presentation may depend on application, so this is just dependency wiring. Both handler methods pull fields out of the request DTO and hand the work to the service. The withdraw handler only wraps the boolean the service returns into a response object. The controller makes no business decision itself: it doesn't work out eligibility, refunds or enrolment rules. It also does no direct database or other I/O. No deterministic checks raised any flags.
